meta.project: Integrated ESG-ABSA Intelligence Framework (v-1 to v3)
meta.description: Consolidated research mapping linking five-layer integrated ESG objectives to technical contributions, research questions, and validated empirical evidence from the NAACL-2025 and thesis evaluation corpus.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: NOVA-63: Native Omni-lingual Versatile Assessments of 63 Disciplines
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports C3 by providing a native multilingual benchmark that avoids 'translationese', essential for validating cross-lingual transfer in bilingual ESG systems.

literature_references.title: WangchanThaiInstruct: An instruction-following Dataset for Culture-Aware, Multitask, and Multi-domain Evaluation in Thai
literature_references.relevance: Provides evidence for RQ1.3 by demonstrating that native, culturally-grounded datasets outperform translated data in model alignment for regional contexts.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?

literature_references.title: SWAN: An Efficient and Scalable Approach for Long-Context Language Modeling
literature_references.relevance: Addresses RQ2.2 and C13 by introducing an architecture that generalizes to long sequences without positional encoding drift, enabling scalable processing of long ESG reports.

literature_references.title: DSMoE: Matrix-Partitioned Experts with Dynamic Routing for Computation-Efficient Dense LLMs
literature_references.relevance: Justifies C10 and RQ2.4 by demonstrating how mixture-of-expert partitioning handles input complexity effectively while maintaining computational efficiency.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?
RQ3.3: How can implicit ESG claims be identified?

literature_references.title: Search-o1: Agentic Search-Enhanced Large Reasoning Models
literature_references.relevance: Links C7 and RQ3.2 by providing a framework for agentic retrieval to resolve reasoning uncertainties in complex, multi-step chains.

literature_references.title: CODI: Compressing Chain-of-Thought into Continuous Space via Self-Distillation
literature_references.relevance: Supports C15 and RQ3.1 by demonstrating how to align natural language CoT with latent spaces, enforcing semantic correctness in reasoning.

research_questions: RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?
RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?

literature_references.title: MPCG: Multi-Round Persona-Conditioned Generation for Modeling the Evolution of Misinformation with LLMs
literature_references.relevance: Directly justifies C11 and RQ4.5 by showing how persona-driven narrative evolution models the drift of claims, mirroring ESG greenwashing behavior.

literature_references.title: SMART: Sycophancy Mitigation Through Reinforcement Learning with Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Reasoning Trajectories
literature_references.relevance: Causally supports C14 and RQ4.1 by providing a mechanism to mitigate model alignment with incorrect user claims, enhancing truthfulness in risk reporting.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: OMS: On-the-fly, Multi-Objective, Self-Reflective Ad Keyword Generation via LLM Agent
literature_references.relevance: Provides evidence for C12 and RQ5.1 by demonstrating a deployment framework that monitors multi-objective performance in real-time environments.

literature_references.title: Jailbreak LLMs through Internal Stance Manipulation
literature_references.relevance: Supports RQ5.2 by identifying latent vulnerabilities in deployed models, stressing the need for auditable safety guardrails in the final platform.
